title: pvRectilinearGridGeometryFilter
body:
## pvRectilinearGridGeometryFilter

Converts a rectilinear grid (vtkRectilinearGrid: axis-aligned cells with separate coordinate arrays along x, y and z) into polygonal data. VTK can restrict this to an i-j-k extent, but ParaView exposes no extent, so the whole grid is used: a 3-D grid becomes a cloud of vertices (one per grid point), a 2-D grid a surface of quadrilaterals and a 1-D grid a polyline, with point and cell data carried over. Use surface or pvExtractSurface to get the outer surface of a 3-D grid instead.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Only vtkRectilinearGrid input works: the ParaView domain accepts any dataset, but the VTK class requires a rectilinear grid, so other inputs fail natively.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `RectilinearGridGeometryFilter`. Identity: `filters/RectilinearGridGeometryFilter`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: Set the input to the Rectilinear Grid Geometry filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |
